references.text: The pillar of cloud moved from in front of the Israelites to behind them and stood between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel.
The Lord looked down on the Egyptian camp from the pillar of fire and cloud and threw them into confusion.
The cloud above the tabernacle guided the Israelites on their journey, with fire in the cloud by night.
By day the cloud covered the tabernacle, and at night it was like fire over it. The cloud led the people on their journey.
The Lord went before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them along the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light.
The Lord went ahead of the people on the road to find places for them to camp, with fire by night and cloud by day.
Nehemiah reminds us that God led the people with a pillar of cloud by day and a pillar of fire by night.
The pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire did not leave them but continued to guide them on their journey.
God guided them with the cloud by day and with the light of fire all through the night.
God spread out a cloud as a covering and gave fire to shine during the night.
Isaiah prophesies about a cloud by day and smoke and flaming fire by night as protection.
Paul refers to how the fathers were under the cloud and were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea.
It expands on the description in Exodus by specifying how the pillar of cloud functioned as a dynamic signal for departure and rest.
It complements the image of the pillar of cloud with the ark of the covenant, showing that both God's presence and His law served as guides.
